hero.headline: Trade & Convention Booths
hero.subheadline: On a crowded show floor, you get three seconds. Beatrox designs and builds trade and convention exhibits that stop traffic, tell your story, and run flawlessly all show long.

body.heading: What is a Trade & Convention Booth Build?
body.content:
A trade or convention booth is a brand's entire world compressed into a few hundred square feet — and Beatrox designs, fabricates, and installs them from Portland, Oregon for exhibitors nationwide. A professional booth build is the design, fabrication, and installation work that makes that footprint outperform everyone around it: structure, graphics, lighting, interactive media, and the logistics of getting it all in and out of a convention hall on a brutal schedule.

You need a purpose-built exhibit when a pipe-and-drape rental can't carry your message: product demos that need integrated displays, experiences that need interactive technology, or a brand presence that has to look unmistakably yours from across the hall. The best booths behave like miniature experiential events.

Convention environments are unforgiving — short install windows, strict union and venue rules, thousands of people leaning on your walls. A booth built by an experienced production team handles all of that quietly, so your staff can focus on the conversations that matter.

body.heading: What BEATROX Provides
body.content:
Beatrox delivers turnkey exhibit builds: design and engineering, custom fabrication, interactive media integration, graphics and signage, show-services coordination, and install/dismantle logistics. Because we're an experiential production company — not just a booth house — our exhibits can include the same LED walls, sensors, and real-time media we build for major events.

For El Camino, we produced a Comic-Con exhibition for Netflix in New York — a high-traffic fan environment where finish quality and durability had to survive constant public interaction across the convention. For the G-MAN Experiential Campaign with Toyota x MTV in Los Angeles, we delivered an experiential event build supporting the campaign's public-facing experience. And our FLIR Interactive History Wall at FLIR's Washington, DC headquarters demonstrates the exhibit-grade side of the craft: an ultra wide-format interactive display with touch-free LIDAR interaction and AI computer vision, engineered for reliability and low maintenance — the same thinking we bring to booths that need to run flawlessly from open to close.

body.heading: How We Work
items: 1. Discovery — We learn your goals, footprint, show rules, and budget
2. Design & Pre-Visualization — See the booth rendered in the actual floor plan before it's built
3. Engineering & Fabrication — Structure, graphics, and interactive elements built and test-fit in the shop
4. Show Logistics — Freight, show services, and venue coordination handled by our team
5. Install & Show Support — We build it on the floor and keep it running all show
6. Dismantle & Storage — Fast teardown, with reusable components crated for the next show

items.question: Can you work within convention center and union rules?
items.answer: Yes. We coordinate show services, labor requirements, and venue regulations as part of every booth project, and we plan install and dismantle around the hall's actual move-in windows.

items.question: Can our booth include interactive technology?
items.answer: Absolutely — that's where we differentiate. Our exhibits can integrate LED walls, touch-free sensors, and real-time media, like the LIDAR-driven interactive history wall we built for FLIR.

items.question: Do you build reusable booths for multiple shows?
items.answer: We design modular systems that break down, crate, and reassemble across a multi-show calendar — protecting your investment and keeping the look consistent city to city.

items.question: How far in advance should we start?
items.answer: Ideally 10–12 weeks before the show for a custom booth, though we've executed on tighter timelines. The earlier we start, the more of the budget goes into the booth itself rather than rush logistics.
